messages:
kevin: Heads-up — product is planning to change default model pin behavior on 2026-04-15. Starting a canary next week. Quick Q: how will pinning + backward-compatibility be communicated? will apps that currently omit a version suddenly see different outputs?

liz: short answer: pinned models (explicit version strings) will keep returning the pinned variant. the change is about the *default* when no version is provided. default will move from a floating alias to an explicit release id after the rollout. :eyes:

arjun: from runtime side: we will add a `model_version` query param and server-side alias -> release mapping. if request is `model=redwood-v1` and no `model_version`, behavior during rollout will be configurable by tenant (sticky vs auto-upgrade). default tenants will be set to sticky for 30 days.

kevin: ok — important for customers who rely on exact logits. do we have an SDK impact matrix? james?

james: SDK change: add optional `model_version` field in all language SDKs + default behavior docstring. we should not change request/response shape. only new query param. minimal churn.

sophia: comms ask: need clear deprecation timeline and migration guide. propose: announce 2026-03-25, docs + SDK patch 2026-03-30, canary 2026-04-01, general rollout 2026-04-15, full sticky-off opt-in 2026-05-15. thoughts?

arjun: timeline sounds fine. runtime tasks: alias mapping service, per-tenant override flag, schema validation for `model_version`. will need a fallback policy for incompatible releases.

liz: small but crucial API contract note — streaming chunks will remain identical (we won't add/remove fields). the only breaking surface is if customers rely on model semantics changing with the alias. recommend adding a `x-model-release` header in responses while canarying so clients can detect the exact release: e.g. `x-model-release: redwood-v1@2026-04-01`.

kevin: good call. add to acceptance criteria. also, let's include an opt-in header for early adopters: `x-model-autoupgrade: true`.

arjun: implemented a prototype locally. example request/response for non-streaming:

```
POST /v1/generate
{ "model": "redwood-v1" }

200 OK
{ "model": "redwood-v1", "model_version": "2026-04-01", "id": "gen_123", "choices": [...] }
```

liz: that JSON shape includes new `model_version` in response — non-breaking if optional. please ensure clients ignore unknown fields. we'll add it to the SDKs too.

sophia: comms: who owns customer notification? propose PM + account teams + an in-console banner for tenants that haven't pinned models. action: I will draft the announcement by 3/25.

james: devex checklist: update SDKs, add migration guide sample showing how to pin `model_version`, add unit tests for ignoring unknown fields, update changelog. I can take the SDK PRs.

arjun: ops checklist: canary deployment lanes, metric for regressed output (we'll diff token distributions), `x-model-release` header toggles, rollout rollback plan. tagging @deploy-bot to schedule canary.

deploy-bot: Scheduled canary: 2026-04-01 09:00 UTC -> eng-platform-canary; rollout window 72h. Notifying owners: @arjun, @liz.

kevin: thanks everyone. action items summary:
- sophia: announcement draft 2026-03-25
- james: SDK PRs + changelog 2026-03-30
- arjun: runtime alias mapping + canary 2026-04-01
- liz: add `x-model-release` header and acceptance tests 2026-03-30
- kevin: coordinate customer comms and enterprise outreach 2026-03-26

liz: also, small API contract Q: do we want to return both `model` and `model_version` in streaming partials? or just final? my vote: include `model_version` in initial stream metadata (first message) so clients can start deterministically.

arjun: agree. will emit stream init event: { "type":"metadata", "model_version":"2026-04-01" } before tokens. non-breaking.

sophia: ok locking that behavior for the doc. I'll include a FAQ covering how tenants can opt to pin, and what happens to open-source integrations.

kevin: if anyone has objections to timeline or behavior, speak now. otherwise I'll mark this thread as the source of truth for rollout decisions. :thumbsup:

liz: no objections. going to open the runtime PR and include tests for backward compatibility.

arjun: will push canary config and smoke-tests by EOD.

james: starting SDK branches. will ping for reviews.

kevin: thanks — closing the loop here. we can move detailed PR links into the thread when they exist.
